          "dependency_level": 1,
          "statement": "Let $(X,d_X)$ and $(\\mathsf Y,d_Y)$ be metric spaces, let $U\\subseteq X$ be a nonempty class of admissible truths, and let $q:U\\to Q$ assign each truth its recovery target in a metric space $(Q,d_Q)$. Let $\\mathfrak A$ index forward maps $F_A:U\\to\\mathsf Y$; in this definition an **operator** means such a forward map, and linearity is not assumed. A specified set $\\mathcal C\\subseteq U\\times\\mathfrak A$ records which truth/operator pairs are admissible; no full-product assumption is made. Equip $\\mathsf Y$ with a sigma-algebra $\\mathcal Y$ and an addition operation such that every translation $\\tau_z(e)=z+e$ is measurable. A **noise law** is a probability measure $\\nu$ on $(\\mathsf Y,\\mathcal Y)$. For each admissible pair $(x,A)\\in\\mathcal C$, the observation random element on the probability space $(\\mathsf Y,\\mathcal Y,\\nu)$ is $e\\mapsto F_A(x)+e$, and its sampling law is\n$$P_{x,A,\\nu}(B)=\\nu\\bigl(\\{e\\in\\mathsf Y:F_A(x)+e\\in B\\}\\bigr),\\qquad B\\in\\mathcal Y.$$\nThe translation measurability assumption makes this law a probability measure.\n\nFor a true specification $(x_\\star,A_\\star,\\nu_\\star)$ with $(x_\\star,A_\\star)\\in\\mathcal C$ and a specified working operator $\\widetilde A\\in\\mathfrak A$ and noise law $\\widetilde\\nu$, there is **operator mismatch at the truth** when $F_{A_\\star}(x_\\star)\\ne F_{\\widetilde A}(x_\\star)$, and there is **noise-law mismatch** when $\\nu_\\star\\ne\\widetilde\\nu$. A **working statistical model** is a metric index space $(\\Xi,d_\\Xi)$, a family $(Q_\\xi)_{\\xi\\in\\Xi}$ of sampling laws on the same data space, and a prior probability measure $\\Pi$ on a sigma-algebra containing every open metric ball. Viewing $\\Phi$ via the inclusion $(-\\infty,+\\infty]\\hookrightarrow\\overline{\\mathbb R}$, it is also product-measurable as an extended-real-valued map because for every Borel set $B\\subseteq\\overline{\\mathbb R}$, $\\Phi^{-1}(B)=\\Phi^{-1}(B\\cap(-\\infty,+\\infty])$ is measurable by the definition of the trace sigma-algebra. Here $+\\infty$ is allowed and $-\\infty$ is excluded; set $e^{-\\infty}=0$. The scalar map $t\\mapsto e^{-t}$ on this range is continuous at finite $t$, and is continuous at $+\\infty$: given $\\varepsilon>0$, the limit supplies $a\\in\\mathbb R$ such that $t>a$ implies $e^{-t}<\\varepsilon$, and the order-topology neighborhood $(a,+\\infty]$ maps into $[0,\\varepsilon)$. Hence it is Borel, so $L_\\Phi:D\\times\\mathsf Y\\to[0,+\\infty)$, $L_\\Phi(u;y):=e^{-\\Phi(u;y)}$, is product-measurable by composition, and each section $u\\mapsto L_\\Phi(u;y)$ is nonnegative and measurable.         {
          "id": "def-ip-posterior-computation-error-budget",
          "kind": "definition",
          "title": "Posterior computation error budget",
          "statement": "Fix a measurable space $(E,\\mathcal E)$ and a bounded measurable functional\n$f:E\\to\\mathbb R$, with $\\|f\\|_\\infty:=\\sup_{x\\in E}|f(x)|<\\infty$. All\ntarget laws below are probability measures on this same space. If a model or\ndiscretization originally uses another state space, specify its measurable\nembedding into $E$ and compare its pushforward law; no identification of\ndifferent state spaces is implicit. A **posterior law** here is the probability\nlaw for the unknown at the specified computation stage, conditional on the same\nfixed observed data. For a probability law $\\mu$, write\n$\\mu(f):=\\int_E f\\,d\\mu$.\n\nName the successive posterior laws as follows: $\\mu_\\star$ is the intended\ntarget; $\\mu_{\\rm model}$ is the posterior under the selected statistical or\nphysical model; $\\mu_{\\rm solver}$ is the posterior after replacing the exact\nforward or PDE solution by the declared numerical solver output; and\n$\\mu_{\\rm disc}$ is the posterior after the declared finite-dimensional\ndiscretization. These labels refer to the exact adjacent laws recorded for the\ncomputation, even when two stages happen to agree.\n\nLet $K$ be the implemented probability kernel on $(E,\\mathcal E)$. An\n**invariant law** $\\pi_K$ for $K$ is a probability measure satisfying\n$$\\int_E K(x,A)\\,\\pi_K(dx)=\\pi_K(A)\\qquad(A\\in\\mathcal E).$$\nChoose and report which invariant law is used if $K$ has more than one. If no\ninvariant law has been established, the invariant-kernel and burn-in terms\nbelow are unavailable; they are not set to zero. Let $(X_n)_{n\\ge0}$ be a\ntime-homogeneous Markov chain with transition kernel $K$ relative to its\nnatural filtration, with initial probability law $\\lambda$. For burn-in length\n$b\\in\\{0,1,2,\\ldots\\}$ and retained sample size $N\\in\\{1,2,3,\\ldots\\}$, set\n$$\\bar f_{b,N}:=\\frac1N\\sum_{j=1}^N f(X_{b+j}),$$\nand let $\\mathbb E_\\lambda$ denote expectation under this initial law and the\nchain's transition randomness.\n\nWhen all stages are present, define the component errors\n$$\\begin{aligned}\\delta_{\\rm model}&:=|\\mu_\\star(f)-\\mu_{\\rm model}(f)|,\\\\ \\delta_{\\rm solver}&:=|\\mu_{\\rm model}(f)-\\mu_{\\rm solver}(f)|,\\\\ \\delta_{\\rm disc}&:=|\\mu_{\\rm solver}(f)-\\mu_{\\rm disc}(f)|,\\\\ \\delta_K&:=|\\mu_{\\rm disc}(f)-\\pi_K(f)|,\\\\ \\delta_{\\rm burn}&:=|\\pi_K(f)-\\mathbb E_\\lambda\\bar f_{b,N}|,\\\\ \\delta_{\\rm MC}&:=|\\mathbb E_\\lambda\\bar f_{b,N}-\\bar f_{b,N}|.\\end{aligned}$$\nThe last component is random and the earlier components are fixed for the\ndeclared data and computation.           "statement": "Assume the Axiom of Choice. Suppose $T:\\mathbb R^d\\times\\mathbb R^m\\to\\mathbb R^d\\times\\mathbb R^m$ is Borel and triangular, $T(x,y)=(T_y(x),y)$, with each $T_y$ a Borel bijection, and define the image measure by $T_{\\#}\\mu(E):=\\mu(T^{-1}(E))$. If\n$$T_{\\#}(\\eta\\otimes\\pi_Y)=\\pi,$$\nthen $T_y{}_{\\#}\\eta=\\pi_y$ as probability measures for $\\pi_Y$-almost every $y$.           "statement": "Assume the Axiom of Choice. Every callable must return its specified value or a failure status in finite time. Any randomization used by these callables is part of the declared input.\n\n**Training and optimizer instructions.** Draw $n$ independent triples\n$$(t_i,X_{0i},(X_{1i},Y_i))\\sim\\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]\\otimes\\eta\\otimes\\pi,$$\nand form $X_{t_i}=(1-t_i)X_{0i}+t_iX_{1i}$ and $V_i=X_{1i}-X_{0i}$. Let $\\mathcal D_n=((t_i,X_{t_i},Y_i,V_i))_{i=1}^n$ and evaluate the empirical squared loss\n$$\\widehat{\\mathcal L}_n(\\theta)=\\frac1n\\sum_{i=1}^n\\bigl|v_\\theta(t_i,X_{t_i},Y_i)-V_i\\bigr|^2.$$\nIf sampling fails, return **sampling-failed**. Otherwise call $\\mathrm{Init}$; if it fails or returns a parameter outside $\\Theta$, return **optimizer-failed** with no fitted field. Set $k=0$ and repeat the following steps in order: evaluate $\\widehat{\\mathcal L}_n(\\theta_k)$ and $S(k,\\theta_k,\\widehat{\\mathcal L}_n,\\mathcal D_n)$; if either evaluation fails or either value is nonfinite, return **optimizer-failed** with no fitted field; if $S\\le\\varepsilon_{\\rm opt}$, stop with status **converged**; if $k=M$, stop with status **budget-exhausted**; otherwise call $\\mathrm{Update}(k,\\theta_k,\\widehat{\\mathcal L}_n,\\mathcal D_n)$, returning **optimizer-failed** with no fitted field if the call fails, returns a parameter outside $\\Theta$, or yields a nonfinite value, and then set $\\theta_{k+1}$ to its output and increase $k$ by one. For either successful stopping status, return $\\widehat v=v_{\\theta_k}$, its achieved training loss, the last value of $S$, $k$, $M$, $\\varepsilon_{\\rm opt}$ and the optimizer status. A finite-data stopping status does not certify $\\widehat v=v^*$.\n\nThe population least-squares target is the conditional-expectation class\n$$v^*(t,x,y)=\\mathbb E[X_1-X_0\\mid\\sigma(t,X_t,Y)]$$\ncoordinatewise, evaluated at $(t,x,y)$ through a chosen measurable representative. A conditional expectation is only an almost-sure equivalence class, so this formula does not specify an off-support pointwise extension.\n\n**Flow and sampling instructions.** For a query datum $y$, call the flow checker on $\\widehat v$ and the data-parameter domain containing $y$. It returns **pass** only when it certifies all hypotheses of the ODE flow lemma, including joint continuity and the integrable global spatial-Lipschitz and origin-growth bounds on compact data-parameter sets containing $y$. If it does not return pass, return **field-regularity-failed** with the optimizer record and no terminal samples. Otherwise, for $j=1,\\ldots,B$, draw independent $Z_0^j\\sim\\eta$ and call the declared solver to integrate on $0\\le t\\le1$\n$$\\dot Z_t^j=\\widehat v(t,Z_t^j,y),\\qquad Z_0^j,$$\nwith budget $h$. Also record each status and any certified solver error estimate, marking an unavailable estimate unquantified. Continue through all $B$ calls after a solver failure. Finite regression loss, optimizer termination, and solver success alone do not establish this joint pushforward identity or exact posterior sampling. Record posterior model, discretization, kernel, burn-in, Monte Carlo and solver components under the declared posterior-computation error budget when applicable.           "statement": "Assume the Axiom of Choice. Its implications supply Dependent Choice and Countable Choice for the finite-dimensional ODE flow assumptions.\n\nLet $\\mathcal H$ be a separable real Hilbert space, let $K\\subseteq\\mathbb R^m$ be compact, and let $y\\mapsto\\Pi^y$ be the pointwise potential posterior of a proper Bayesian inverse model, with positive finite evidence and finite second moment for every $y\\in K$. For a measurable vector field $v:\\,[0,1]\\times\\mathcal H_n\\times K\\to\\mathcal H_n$, define its pointwise conditional population loss by\n$$\\mathcal L_{n,y}(v):=\\int_0^1\\mathbb E\\!\\left[\\left\\|v(t,P_nX_t,y)-P_n(X_1-X_0)\\right\\|_{\\mathcal H}^2\\mid Y=y\\right]dt,$$\nusing the selected conditional-law version.           "statement": "Let $X,Y$ be real Hilbert spaces, let $U\\subseteq X$ be open, and let $F:U\\to Y$ be Fréchet differentiable at every point with a derivative map $F':U\\to\\mathcal B(X,Y)$ that is continuous in operator norm. This is the real-Hilbert forward-map convention. Assume Countable Choice, so every bounded derivative $F'(x)$ has the Hilbert adjoint $F'(x)^*:Y\\to X$ characterized by $\\langle F'(x)u,v\\rangle_Y=\\langle u,F'(x)^*v\\rangle_X$.\n\nAn **admissible local instance** consists of an initial point $x_0\\in U$, a radius $r>0$, an exact solution $x^\\dagger\\in\\overline B_r(x_0):=\\{x\\in X:\\|x-x_0\\|_X\\le r\\}$ with exact datum $y=F(x^\\dagger)$, a noise level $\\delta\\ge0$, noisy datum $y^\\delta\\in Y$ with $\\|y^\\delta-y\\|_Y\\le\\delta$, a constant $0\\le\\eta<1/2$, a discrepancy parameter $\\tau>2(1+\\eta)/(1-2\\eta)$, and a finite update budget $M\\in\\mathbb N_0$. The closed outer ball $\\overline B_{2r}(x_0)$ is contained in $U$; $\\|F'(x)\\|\\le1$ for every $x\\in\\overline B_{2r}(x_0)$; and the uniform two-point tangential-cone inequality\n\n$$\n\\|F(x)-F(\\widetilde x)-F'(x)(x-\\widetilde x)\\|_Y\\le\\eta\\|F(x)-F(\\widetilde x)\\|_Y\n$$\n\nholds for every $x,\\widetilde x\\in\\overline B_{2r}(x_0)$. This is the uniform family of the one-basepoint local tangential-cone inequality; the shared constant and pair domain are part of the admissibility hypothesis. The exact solution and the bounds are analysis data and need not be available to the computational loop.\n\n**Inputs:** $F$, $x_0$, $y^\\delta$, $\\delta$, $\\tau$, and $M$ from an admissible local instance.\n\n**Output:** Either `stopped` with an index $k$, iterate $x_k^\\delta$, and residual $\\|y^\\delta-F(x_k^\\delta)\\|_Y$, or `budget_exhausted` with the last iterate and its residual.\n\n**Procedure:** Set $x_0^\\delta:=x_0$. For $k=0,1,\\ldots,M$, compute $r_k^\\delta:=\\|y^\\delta-F(x_k^\\delta)\\|_Y$. If $r_k^\\delta\\le\\tau\\delta$, return `stopped` with $(k,x_k^\\delta,r_k^\\delta)$. If $k=M$, return `budget_exhausted` with $(k,x_k^\\delta,r_k^\\delta)$. Otherwise set\n\n$$\nx_{k+1}^\\delta:=x_k^\\delta+F'(x_k^\\delta)^*(y^\\delta-F(x_k^\\delta))\n$$\n\nand continue at the next index.           "statement": "Let $X,Y$ be real Hilbert spaces, let $U\\subseteq X$ be open, and let $F:U\\to Y$ be Fréchet differentiable at every point with $F':U\\to\\mathcal B(X,Y)$ continuous in operator norm. Fix $x_0\\in U$ and $r>0$ such that $\\overline B_{2r}(x_0)\\subseteq U$, and suppose an exact solution $x^\\dagger\\in\\overline B_r(x_0)$ satisfies $y=F(x^\\dagger)$. Assume $\\|F'(x)\\|\\le1$ for every $x\\in\\overline B_{2r}(x_0)$ and that, for some $0\\le\\eta<1/2$,\n\n$$\n\\|F(x)-F(\\widetilde x)-F'(x)(x-\\widetilde x)\\|_Y\\le\\eta\\|F(x)-F(\\widetilde x)\\|_Y\n$$\n\nfor every $x,\\widetilde x\\in\\overline B_{2r}(x_0)$. This is a uniform two-point hypothesis with the derivative based at the first point. Assume Countable Choice so that the bounded derivatives have Hilbert adjoints. For $\\delta\\ge0$ and $y^\\delta\\in Y$ with $\\|y^\\delta-y\\|_Y\\le\\delta$, set $x_0^\\delta=x_0$ and define the ideal Landweber sequence by\n\n$$\nx_{n+1}^\\delta=x_n^\\delta+F'(x_n^\\delta)^*(y^\\delta-F(x_n^\\delta)).\n$$\n\nLet $\\tau>2(1+\\eta)/(1-2\\eta)$. For $\\delta>0$, let $N(\\delta,y^\\delta)$ denote the first $n\\in\\mathbb N_0$ with $\\|y^\\delta-F(x_n^\\delta)\\|_Y\\le\\tau\\delta$, if it exists. Put $d_0=\\|x_0-x^\\dagger\\|_X$ and $c_\\tau=1-2\\eta-2(1+\\eta)/\\tau>0$. Then the following hold.\n\n1. For every update before the first discrepancy stop, writing $R_n^\\delta=\\|y^\\delta-F(x_n^\\delta)\\|_Y$, the squared-error estimate is\n\n   $$\n   \\|x_{n+1}^\\delta-x^\\dagger\\|_X^2-\\|x_n^\\delta-x^\\dagger\\|_X^2\\le R_n^\\delta\\bigl(2(1+\\eta)\\delta-(1-2\\eta)R_n^\\delta\\bigr).\n   $$\n\n   In particular, the iterates are Fejér monotone relative to $x^\\dagger$ up to the stop: their distance to $x^\\dagger$ does not increase. If $\\delta>0$, the first discrepancy index exists and\n\n   $$\n   N(\\delta,y^\\delta)<C\\delta^{-2},\\qquad C:=1+\\frac{d_0^2}{c_\\tau\\tau^2}.\n   $$\n\n   A run of the finite-budget algorithm with budget $M\\ge N(\\delta,y^\\delta)$ returns `stopped` at this first index; if $M<N(\\delta,y^\\delta)$, it returns `budget_exhausted` at $M$.\n\n3. No finite stopping index is claimed in the exact-data case.\n\n4.           "statement": "Assume the Axiom of Choice.           "statement": "Let $(X,d_X)$ and $(Y,d_Y)$ be metric parameter and data spaces, let $U\\subseteq X$ be a nonempty admissible truth class, let $F:U\\to Y$ be a forward map, and let $(Q,d_Q)$ be a metric target space. All metric spaces in this definition carry their Borel sigma-algebras. Give $U$ the subspace Borel sigma-algebra $\\mathcal B(U):=\\{U\\cap A:A\\in\\mathcal B(X)\\}$, and assume that $q:U\\to Q$ is measurable from $(U,\\mathcal B(U))$ to $(Q,\\mathcal B(Q))$. The target $q(x)$ is the recovery object assigned to truth $x$; $Q$ may be the parameter space itself or a quotient solution-class space. A **point reconstruction rule** is a Borel map $g:Y\\to Q$, and its output at data $y$ is $g(y)$. A **learned point estimator** is such a map $\\widehat q_\\phi$ with a fitted parameter $\\phi$ in a specified parameter set. A complete training description names the probability law $P_{\\rm fit}$ of all variables used to fit $\\phi$; those variables may be paired or unpaired. A complete test description names a probability law $P_{\\rm test}$ for evaluation pairs $(Y,q(X))$. No equality between fitting and test laws is assumed.\n\nA finite **unrolled learned update** consists of an integer $K\\geq1$, a Borel initialization $u_0:Y\\to Q$, and maps $T_{\\phi,k}:Q\\times Y\\to Q$ measurable from $(Q\\times Y,\\mathcal B(Q)\\otimes\\mathcal B(Y))$ to $(Q,\\mathcal B(Q))$ for $0\\leq k<K$, with $u_{k+1}(y)=T_{\\phi,k}(u_k(y),y)$. Here the layer domain uses the product sigma-algebra, not an assumed identification with the Borel sigma-algebra of the product topology. Its output $u_K:Y\\to Q$ is a point reconstruction rule: if $u_k$ is Borel, the preimage of a measurable rectangle $A\\times C$ under $y\\mapsto(u_k(y),y)$ is $u_k^{-1}(A)\\cap C$, so this pairing is product-measurable; composing it with $T_{\\phi,k}$ and applying finite induction proves that every $u_k$ is Borel. An **amortized inverse map** is a learned point estimator applied to multiple data inputs after a single fit; this term adds a reuse convention, not an accuracy guarantee.\n\nFor a real Hilbert signal space $H$, a **denoiser** is a Borel map $D_\\phi:H\\to H$ trained under a specified signal-corruption law and used to transform a corrupted signal into a signal estimate or an update. A denoiser is the exact minimum mean-square error map only when it equals the conditional mean for the specified signal and corruption laws. A **learned prior** is a supplied Borel probability measure $\\rho_\\phi$ on $H$; one construction is the pushforward law $\\rho_\\phi(A)=\\nu(G_\\phi^{-1}(A))$ for $A\\in\\mathcal B(H)$, where $\\nu$ is a specified probability measure on a measurable source space $(Z,\\mathcal Z)$ and $G_\\phi:(Z,\\mathcal Z)\\to(H,\\mathcal B(H))$ is measurable. The law or generator alone is not a data-to-target estimator.\n\nFor a finite horizon $T>0$, a specified parameter set $\\Phi$, and $\\phi\\in\\Phi$, a **score field model** in a finite-dimensional signal space $\\mathbb R^d$ is a Borel map $s_\\phi:[0,T]\\times\\mathbb R^d\\to\\mathbb R^d$ intended to approximate the target field $s^*(t,x)=\\nabla_x\\log p_t(x)$ for a specified family $(p_t)_{t\\in[0,T]}$ of positive continuously differentiable probability densities for which $s^*$ is jointly Borel. Its complete description names a probability law $P_{\\rm fit}$ for all variables used to fit $\\phi$ and a probability law $P_{\\rm test}$ on $[0,T]\\times\\mathbb R^d$ for evaluation inputs $(t,x)$; the target on those inputs is $s^*(t,x)$. These laws need not agree, and no approximation guarantee under either law is implied. A score field is not itself a posterior law, posterior sample, or point reconstruction rule. A **posterior sampler** is a probability kernel $S:Y\\to Q$; relative to a supplied posterior target kernel $\\Pi_y$, it is exact on a data domain $D$ when $S_y=\\Pi_y$ as probability measures for every $y\\in D$.           "statement": "Fix measurable spaces $(X,\\mathcal X)$ and $(Y,\\mathcal Y)$, a metric target space $(Q,d_Q)$ with its Borel sigma-algebra $\\mathcal Q$, and a nonempty truth class $U\\subseteq X$ with inherited sigma-algebra $\\mathcal U=\\{A\\cap U:A\\in\\mathcal X\\}$.           "statement": "Zheng et al.'s InverseBench reports 14 plug-and-play diffusion-prior algorithms and domain-specific baselines on five selected cases: first-Born optical scattering, raw multi-coil knee MRI, black-hole very-long-baseline interferometry, full waveform inversion, and two-dimensional vorticity-form Navier–Stokes inversion. In cases with closed-form forward models, methods using more forward-gradient queries can be more accurate and more expensive; the paper reports that this trend fails for its numerical PDE cases. Its Figure 5 out-of-distribution diagnostics feed digit images to a black-hole prior trained on simulated black-hole images, and nine-cell scattering sources to a prior trained on one-to-six-cell sources; for the black-hole case, the authors report outputs with the prior's characteristic ring feature.           "statement": "Let $F$ be a compact oriented embedded surface in the oriented $3$-sphere. An **embedded arc surgery** on $F$ is the following operation. Require the lateral annulus $[0,1]\\times\\partial D^2$ to admit an orientation agreeing along both attaching circles with the orientation on the remaining part of $F$. Replace the two disks by that annulus, then round the two seams in disjoint neighbourhoods of the attaching circles to obtain a smooth embedded surface $F_C$. The core $[0,1]\\times\\{0\\}$ is the surgery arc. The operation preserves $\\partial F$ and its boundary orientation; its reverse is called an arc-surgery reduction.\n\n```tikz\n\\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.95,>=stealth]\n  \\draw[thick] (-3,0) .. controls (-2.4,0.65) and (-1.8,0.65) ..           "statement": "Let $V=S^1\\times D^2$ be the standard oriented solid torus, with oriented core $S^1\\times\\{0\\}$. A **pattern** is a smooth oriented knot $P$ contained in the interior of $V$, together with a chosen closed tubular neighbourhood $N(P)$ contained in the interior of $V$. Its **winding number** $w(P)$ is the integer by which the homology class $[P]$ maps to $H_1(V;\\mathbb Z)\\cong\\mathbb Z$ under the isomorphism that sends the oriented core to $1$. The **pattern exterior** is $X_P=V\\setminus\\operatorname{int}N(P)$; its **outer torus** is $\\partial V$ and its **inner torus** is $\\partial N(P)$. A **companion** is a smooth oriented knot $K\\subset S^3$ with a specified orientation-preserving tubular embedding $e:V\\to S^3$ that sends the core to $K$ and identifies the solid-torus meridian and product longitude with the positive meridian and preferred longitude of $K$. The **satellite knot** $P(K)$ is $e(P)$, with chosen exterior $E_{P(K)}=S^3\\setminus\\operatorname{int}e(N(P))$; the image $e(\\partial V)$ is its **companion torus**. The outer torus is **incompressible** when it bounds no properly embedded disk in $X_P$ with essential boundary on $\\partial V$. It is **product-parallel** to the inner torus when $X_P$ is a product $T^2\\times[0,1]$ with those tori as its ends. This definition alone asserts neither incompressibility nor essentiality of the companion torus."

          "statement": "Let $M$ be a compact smooth $3$-manifold. A properly embedded surface is **two-sided** if it has a product neighbourhood $F\\times[-1,1]$ in $M$. A **compressing disk** for a two-sided surface $F$ is an embedded disk $D\\subset M$ with $\\operatorname{int}(D)\\cap F=\\varnothing$ and $\\partial D$ an essential simple closed curve in $F$; $F$ is **incompressible** if it has no compressing disk. A **boundary-compressing disk** is an embedded disk $D$ with $\\partial D=\\alpha\\cup\\beta$, where $\\alpha=D\\cap F$ is an arc not cutting off a disk in $F$, $\\beta=D\\cap\\partial M$, and $\\operatorname{int}(D)$ misses $F\\cup\\partial M$; $F$ is **boundary-incompressible** if it has no such disk. A surface is **boundary-parallel** if it cobounds a product with a subsurface of $\\partial M$, and it is **essential** if it is incompressible, boundary-incompressible, and not boundary-parallel. $M$ is **irreducible** if every embedded $2$-sphere in its interior bounds an embedded $3$-ball in $M$. An incompressible torus is boundary-parallel if it cobounds a product $T^2\\times[0,1]$ with a component of $\\partial M$; $M$ is **atoroidal** if every incompressible torus is boundary-parallel. A **Seifert fibration** is a decomposition into circles with local models given by fibered solid tori; in the model $(D^2\\times S^1)/\\langle(z,w)\\mapsto(e^{2\\pi i/q}z,e^{2\\pi ip/q}w)\\rangle$, where $\\gcd(p,q)=1$, the core fiber has multiplicity $q$. Fibers of multiplicity $1$ are **regular** and those of multiplicity greater than $1$ are **exceptional**. A finite family of pairwise disjoint incompressible tori is a **JSJ system** if every component obtained by cutting $M$ along the family is atoroidal or Seifert-fibered. It is **inclusion-minimal** if no proper subfamily is a JSJ system. Atoroidal does not mean hyperbolic."

the oriented link components. A code is **connected** when the graph with
vertices $C$ and edges the $\alpha$-pairs is connected.

$\det(v_{\rm over},v_{\rm under})$ is positive or negative, where the two
tangent vectors follow the oriented over- and under-strands. This item fixes
the local cyclic-order convention as follows. Starting with the outgoing

rectangular edge band for each pair of darts under $\alpha$, and one cap disk

pair, and sign. `components` lists the oriented link cycles, `faces` lists the

selected face gives the plane model. The procedure tests realizability of
